3. Defendant Nos.1-2 contested the suit by filing joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs are not valid sons of Joshoda and as such, they are not reversioners of Raj Mohan. Raj Mohan had two daughters, namely Joshoda, mother of the plaintiffs and Kumali, mother of Kali Kanta and wife of Gangadhar. Joshoda was married to Umakanta Das. But Umakanta Das died just after the marriage. Then, Joshoda came back to her father's house and at that time she was childless. Thereafter, she was abducted by one Abdul Matin Talukder. Thus, she lost her chastity. After recovery, she was kept under the care of Khirodhar Karmaker. Thereafter, Joshoda never married Khiridhor Karmaker according to Hindu religion. She was treated like a slave (dashi). The plaintiffs are illegitimate sons of Joshoda and Khiridhor. Raj Kanta died leaving behind wife Konok Prova, mother Furkuni and one nephew Kali Kanta. After the death of Raj Kanta, Konok Prova became the owner of the suit land with life interest. She sold the suit land to Subarna Lata and Sandhya Ranni by registered kabala dated 11.10.1946 for legal necessity. Sometimes after the kabala was registered, Konok Prova was kidnapped by an unruly person and she was forced to embraced Islam. Subsequently, there was a quarrel between Furkuni and Kali Kanta over the suit land. There was a salish and as per the salish, Furkuni and Kali Kanta jointly executed and registered another kabala dated 14.12.1946 in favour of Subarna Lata and Sandhya Rani. Thus, they acquired right and title in the suit property. Subarna Lata and Sandhya Rani settled the suit land in favour of different persons including defendant Nos.1 and 3. Accordingly, S.A. Khatian was prepared in their names. 

 4. Defendant Nos.7-19 contested the suit by filing another joint written statement contending, inter alia, that Sandhya Rani settled .06 acre of land from Plot No.1555 in favour of Nuta Shah and accordingly R.S. Khatian No.476 was prepared in the name of Nuta Shah. The plaintiffs purchased .06 acre of land by registered kabala dated 29.11.1973 from Yeasin and Siddique Ali. The plaintiffs also got settlement of 2.40 acres of land from Subarna Lata and Sandhya Ranni by a registered kabuliyat dated 04.02.1956 A.D. After selling some lands, the plaintiffs also possessed 1.84 acres of land. Accordingly, their names were recorded in S.A. Khatian No.481. As S.A. Khatian No.480 was prepared in the name of Rohini in respect of .15 acre of land, the plaintiffs obtained a declaration of title in Other Class Suit No.492 of 1969 from the Court of Munsif, Gaibandha and whereupon they also got their names mutated and got S.A. Khatian No.481 corrected in Miscellaneous Case No.70 of 1977-78. Therefore, there took place several sale and subsequent sales after 1946 and accordingly, S.A. Khatian Nos.479, 477, 474, 478 and 766 were prepared. Both Furkuni and Konok Prova visited Goya Dham. Furkuni died in 1966. After the death of Furkuni, the plaintiffs are not the next reversioners of Raj Kanta. Gimio Mohin Das and Ramananda Das left Bangladesh for India long before the independence of Bangladesh. The plaintiffs cannot get relief as prayed for, because they have taken pattan from Subarna Lata and Sandhya Rani and also purchased some lands from their heirs Nuta Shah. As such, the plaintiff's suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
